notes: Reached via Claude-in-Chrome only (own tab, no other route). robots.txt (fetched 2026-08-24) has no Claude-specific full-site Disallow; the default group's Disallow list (/account/*, /accounts/*, /log-in*, /sign-up*, /tracking*, /checkout/thank-you*, /p/*, /partner/*) does not touch /shop/home/* category pages, consistent with this project's prior-pass precedent that this is not a block. Furniture department found via homepage nav: quince.com/shop/home/furniture (top-level 'furniture' link), which is itself a grouping page aggregating 4 room departments shown in its COLLECTION_NAV_CAROUSEL widget: Living Room Furniture, Bedroom Furniture, Dining Room Furniture, Outdoor Furniture (site's own pageDataJson.widgets, read via same-origin access to window.__NEXT_DATA__ in the loaded tab -- confirms Next.js SSR + widget-tree structure noted in the prior Home-Decor pass for this brand). Cross-checked the mandatory sitemap per brief SS7b: quince.com/sitemap.xml -> sitemap_us.xml -> sitemap_shop.xml lists exactly these same 5 furniture URLs (the 4 rooms + the /furniture parent), confirming no hidden top-level furniture department was missed. A second sitemap, sitemap_subcollections.xml, revealed 11 deeper clean-URL subcategory pages NOT surfaced in any on-page nav widget (each room page's own COLLECTION_NAV_CAROUSEL was empty) -- these are the true deepest nodes per the URL hierarchy rule and were used in place of the 4 room pages as leaves, which therefore became grouping rows. Outdoor Furniture has zero subcollection entries in the sitemap (verified) so it remains a leaf itself. QTY METHOD: this brand's platform embeds a PRODUCT_LIST widget (pdj.widgets.find(type==='PRODUCT_LIST')) with pagination.total/limit/hasMore and up to 30 SSR-rendered product cards, each keyed by a stable productId. Per this project's prior Home-Decor pass on this exact brand, pagination.total (matching the on-page 'N items' text) counts one row per product-COLOR variant, not one row per distinct product -- re-verified independently here on every furniture node checked (e.g. Living Room Furniture: total=727 vs only 16 distinct productIds among the visible 30; Sectionals: total=288 vs 19 distinct; Beds: total=105 vs 12 distinct). Per THE ONE RULE, qty=null+flag was used wherever pagination.hasMore=true, since the true distinct-product count cannot be confirmed beyond the visible SSR page (this session's Chrome tab pool was extremely congested -- 40-60 tabs from ~20 parallel sibling workers sharing one browser -- causing frequent renderer freezes/timeouts on repeated same-tab JS calls; scrolling/interacting to trigger the client-side 'load more' fetch for large categories (up to 727 total rows) was not reliable enough in this environment to fully enumerate, so an honest null+flag with a deduplicated floor was used instead of guessing). Where pagination.hasMore=false (small categories fully returned in one SSR page), the deduplicated productId count IS the verified exact distinct-product total and was recorded as qty with no flag: Consoles & Bookshelves=7, Coffee & End Tables=11, Dining Chairs & Stools=11, Dining Tables=9, Dressers & Nightstands=7. 'Leather Furniture' (living-room-furniture/leather-furniture) is included as a leaf but flagged ambiguous: its own page title ('Leather Furniture -- Stillman Sofas, Sectionals & Chairs in Leather') suggests it may be centered on one named product line/collection rather than a pure material-based product-type category; kept because it has its own canonical URL, is listed in the site's official subcollections sitemap alongside the unambiguous product-type nodes, and the Home Decor project's material restrictions explicitly do not apply to this Furniture task. SCOPE EXCLUDED (non-furniture Quince departments, out of scope per brief SS1): Bedding, Bath, Kitchen & Tabletop, Rugs, Curtains, Decor/Wall Art/Mirrors/Planters/Coffee Table Books/Decorative Objects, Candles, Cookware -- none of these overlap with the Furniture nodes recorded here.
